The Company is hopeful to get it approved with suitable modifications, if any.

The outlook for the Infrastructure sector appears positive since the country is looking forward with a strong mandate to stimulate economic growth. Roads, highways, irrigation, industrial infrastructure, and coal handling projects are expected to remain major contributors to the construction and EPC industry over the next decade. With sustained capital expenditure, increasing industrialization, and strong policy push, the Indian infrastructure sector is expected to maintain robust long-term growth with estimated sectorial CAGR ranging between 7% and 12% across major infrastructure segments.

India's ambitious plan calls for spending US$ 1.723 trillion (approximately Rs. 143 trillion) on infrastructure between FY26 and FY30, with a particular emphasis on power, roads, and developing industries like renewable energy and electric vehicles.
India is committed to attaining net-zero carbon emissions by 2070, and the country's ambitious goal of 500 gigawatts (GW) of renewable capacity by 2030 should be met.

risks: Periodic assessments to identify the risk areas are carried out and management is briefed on the risks in advance to enable the Company to control risk through a properly defined plan.
The Company has the major effect on timely completion of various projects.
The availability of construction labor force is expected to affect the projects for some time.

Construction delays continue to be a concern factor which stems from number of factors outside the control of the project sponsors, which includes land acquisition, regulatory approvals, inflation, and litigation etc., which can delay the timely completion of the project and increase in cost of project.
Additional funding, additional cost of fund etc.

As the sector is driven by infrastructure projects to a large extent, it is expected to be hit severely by the current levels of uncertainty, dismal business and consumer sentiments, loss of income as well as the diversion of government funds towards other sectors.
